title: Kill the local cmux-tui under two terminal tabs, send a mutation while the app is disconnected, and converge to the same workspace, tabs and terminals on the new connection
preconditions: a fresh launch: one window, one workspace, one terminal tab, connected to the tag's own cmux-tui

allow_crashes.reason: drop-connection kills the tag's cmux-tui owner on purpose to drop the app's connection

steps.note: the launch's connection to the tag's cmux-tui is up
a second terminal tab, so two terminal hosts outlive the owner

expect.noReceiptReason: a killed process runs no action; the connection state the waitFor reads is the result

steps.note: SIGKILL of the cmux-tui owner (not its terminal hosts): the app sees the connection end and leaves connected; no settle, so the next step goes at once

reaches the app before the next owner is up (server ensure, its restore, then the handshake), so its command finds no connection and the run answers a typed error; the settle after it waits through the reconnect
the app reconnected by itself to a new owner, which adopted the terminal hosts, and has a fresh snapshot
a mutation on the new connection reaches the new owner and comes back in its snapshot

invariants: rename-while-disconnected answers control.daemon_error, and the workspace's name at after-reconnect is the one at before-drop: the mutation sent while disconnected was refused with a typed error, neither dropped silently nor applied later

the crashes facet counts no daemon exit at before-drop and exactly one at after-reconnect: the app names the dropped connection, and every snapshot from after-reconnect on is the next connection's (daemon_state connected); no holder exit
after-reconnect has the workspace, the two terminal tabs and the focused pane of before-drop with the same public ids: the new owner adopted the hosts
no intent is pending at after-reconnect and the rollback counter did not move
rename-after-reconnect changes only the workspace's name
every mutation has one receipt or one typed error (I1)
teardown: quit the tagged app the run started
verify its debug socket is gone
untested: Retry Now on the recovery card (debug.daemon retry): the app reconnects by itself first, so a press would be a no-op here
a delayed (not dropped) connection: the app has no latency injection for its local daemon, and case-v1 kill sends no SIGSTOP
the agent connection: the bench launch's mock agent pane has no connection to drop
the daemon's process generation itself: session.generation is a fresh random value per start (x-oracle-volatile), so the case names the connection by the crashes facet's daemon count and daemon_state
